theorem: In arbitrary finite bipartite dimensions, let A>=0, B>=0 and W=A tensor B-|psi><psi|. If W is product-block-positive, then W^Gamma>=0: W is completely copositive and cannot have negative expectation on ANY PPT state. Conversely W^Gamma>=0 implies product-block-positivity. This includes singular A,B. Consequently even a 2-block-positive witness in this entire product-metric/rank-one-subtraction family, as well as any local congruence or nonnegative sum of its members, cannot certify the requested PPT/SN>=3 pair. This is an elementary structural no-go; no novelty is claimed.
support_proof: For x in ker A and arbitrary y, product-block-positivity gives -|<psi|x tensor y>|^2>=0, so psi is orthogonal to ker A tensor the entire Bob space. Similarly it is orthogonal to the entire Alice space tensor ker B. Thus psi belongs to ran(A) tensor ran(B). If either A or B is zero this forces psi=0 and W=0. Otherwise put S=A^(1/2) tensor B^(1/2) and phi=S^+ psi, so psi=S phi and W=S*(I-|phi><phi|)*S^*. Product-block-positivity on the supports, tested after pseudoinverse local changes of variables, is equivalent to |<phi|x tensor y>|^2<=||x||^2||y||^2 for all product x tensor y. By the Schmidt decomposition, this is exactly s1(phi)^2<=1, where s1 is the largest Schmidt coefficient.
copt_proof: The spectrum of |phi><phi|^Gamma consists of s_i^2 and pairs +/-s_i*s_j, plus possible zeros, so its largest eigenvalue is s1^2<=1. Therefore I-|phi><phi|^Gamma>=0. Taking the Bob transpose of the local congruence gives W^Gamma=(A^(1/2) tensor conjugate(B^(1/2)))*(I-|phi><phi|^Gamma)*(A^(1/2) tensor conjugate(B^(1/2)))^*>=0, valid even for singular factors. Conversely the product expectation of W equals the product expectation of W^Gamma on the conjugated Bob factor, so coCP implies block positivity. For PPT rho, tr(W rho)=tr(W^Gamma rho^Gamma)>=0. Local product congruences and nonnegative sums preserve coCP.
pure_fidelity_corollary: The usual pure-target Schmidt-k fidelity witness W_k=(sum_(i=1)^k s_i(psi)^2)I-|psi><psi| is a special case, and is coCP for every k>=1 because the threshold is at least s1^2. Thus no pure-target fidelity witness alone can detect any PPT state; local filtering and nonnegative sums of such coCP witnesses cannot change this. This covers product metrics only, not arbitrary nonproduct positive offsets or general sums of subtractions.
singular_metric_example: Take A=diag(1,4,0,9), B=diag(4,0,9,1), and phi=(4/5)|00>+(3/5)|12>+(1/2)|33>. With S=A^(1/2) tensor B^(1/2), psi=S phi=(8/5)|00>+(18/5)|12>+(3/2)|33>. The two largest squared Schmidt coefficients of phi sum to1, so I-|phi><phi| and its local congruence W are 2-block-positive. Its squared norm is5/4, and x=(2/5)|00>+(1/10)|12>+(1/6)|33> satisfies <x|W|x>=-5/16, so W itself is not PSD. The exact partial transpose is PSD, illustrating a nontrivial singular-metric 2-positive but coCP case.

exact_check.observed: Fraction arithmetic constructs all256 entries of the singular example, confirms W^Gamma PSD by nonnegative Schur pivots, confirms the rank3 test expectation -5/16, and checks the exact Schmidt-square sums. The universal all-dimensional theorem follows from the written support and PT-eigenvalue proof.

limits: The positive offset must be a SINGLE tensor product A tensor B and the negative term rank1. The result does not classify all 2-positive maps, offsets that are general separable/entangled PSD operators, multiple-subtraction witnesses, or arbitrary 4x4 PPT states. No external/formal review or novelty clearance.
